LESSON: MELODY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.7: Melody
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Melody, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How can one create interesting melodies?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Melody together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: the learner will make thoughtful choices in selecting solfa syllables and note values to combine

using various techniques to compose melodies.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: developed when the learner listens and recognises sol-fa sounds in melodies as well

as in interpretation of hand signs.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematics: Number concept and sequencing learnt in Mathematics is applied in combination of solfa syllables in stepwise

motion and leaps.

• English: Vowels learnt in English are used to sing the solfa syllables ascending and descending.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: developed when the learner listens and recognises sol-fa sounds in melodies as well

as in interpretation of hand signs.

Values:

• Respect: is developed when the learner appreciates and appraises others’ compositions.

• Unity: is achieved through working in groups to produce a melody.

• Integrity: is developed when creating own compositions without copying what other peers have already created.
